items.q: How much does Pipedrive cost per user?
items.a: As of 26 September 2026, Pipedrive has four plans, all billed per seat: Lite at $24 a month, Growth at $49, Premium at $79 and Ultimate at $99, each charged whether or not the seat's assigned user is active. Paying annually lowers every plan: Lite drops to $14 a month, Growth to $39, Premium to $59 and Ultimate to $79. Pipedrive's own pricing page describes this discount as 'up to 42%,' though the real size varies by plan: about 42% on Lite, 20% on Growth, 25% on Premium and 20% on Ultimate. None of these prices include email marketing, which Pipedrive sells separately on every plan through its Campaigns add-on, or feature add-ons like LeadBooster and Smart Docs on the two cheaper plans. A solo rep on Lite who also wants basic email marketing typically pays around $40 a month once that add-on is included, not the $24 sticker price alone.

items.q: Does Pipedrive have a free plan?
items.a: No. Pipedrive has no free-forever plan; the only way to use it without paying is a 14-day free trial, which Pipedrive's pricing page and several feature pages confirm does not require a credit card. The trial gives full access to whichever plan you sign up under, though Prospector lead-reveal credits aren't part of the main trial. Two add-ons run separate, shorter trials of their own: Smart Docs offers its own 14-day add-on trial limited to 5 signature requests, and Web Visitors runs a 7-day trial of real website traffic before Pipedrive assigns it a permanent tier and price. Once any trial ends, the cheapest way to keep using Pipedrive is the Lite plan at $24 a month, or $14 a month on annual billing. There's no reduced-feature free tier to fall back on the way some competing CRMs offer.

items.q: What add-ons does Pipedrive charge extra for?
items.a: Pipedrive sells five separate add-ons on top of its plan price. LeadBooster (chatbot, live chat, web forms and 10 monthly Prospector lead-reveal credits) costs $39 a company a month. Projects, for task and project management, costs $20 per seat a month. Smart Docs, for proposals and e-signatures, starts at $39 a month. Web Visitors, which identifies anonymous website traffic, starts at $49 a month for up to 200 identified organizations and rises in tiers as traffic grows. Campaigns, Pipedrive's email marketing tool, is priced by the number of marketing subscribers you hold, starting at $0.016 per subscriber a month. LeadBooster, Projects and Smart Docs are included at no extra cost for every seat on the Premium and Ultimate plans; only Campaigns and Web Visitors stay separate add-ons no matter which plan you buy. Most of these add-ons also cost less if billed annually instead of month to month.

items.q: Does Pipedrive charge extra for email marketing?
items.a: Yes, on every plan, including the top-tier Ultimate. Campaigns, Pipedrive's email marketing tool, isn't bundled into any plan's price; it's billed separately by the number of marketing subscribers you hold, not by how many emails you send. The Standard tier starts at $0.016 per subscriber a month for your first 1,000 subscribers, then steps down as your list grows, so for exactly 1,000 subscribers the add-on costs $16 a month. A Premium feature tier of Campaigns, with comparative insights and extra filters, costs 1.5 times the Standard rate at every band. Because Campaigns meters subscriber count rather than folding into the subscription, a Pipedrive bill grows with your contact list even when your seat count never changes. A 3-person team holding 5,000 marketing subscribers, for example, pays $42 a month for Campaigns on top of its Growth seats, which is one reason the small-team bill runs to $189 rather than the $147 the seats alone would cost.

items.q: Is Pipedrive cheaper if you pay annually, and can you switch back?
items.a: Yes. As of 26 September 2026, every plan costs less per seat billed annually: Lite drops from $24 to $14 a month, Growth from $49 to $39, Premium from $79 to $59, and Ultimate from $99 to $79. Pipedrive's own copy calls this a discount of 'up to 42%,' though the actual size varies by plan. The trade-off is commitment: annual subscriptions are prepaid for the full year and are not refundable, and canceling one only stops the next renewal, so you keep access through the term you already paid for rather than getting money back. A monthly subscription, by contrast, can be canceled at any time and simply stops billing at the next monthly date. If you're still deciding which plan or which add-ons fit your team, starting on monthly billing and moving to annual later, once you're sure, avoids locking in a full year on a plan you might outgrow.

items.q: Can you get a refund if you cancel Pipedrive?
items.a: Not for an annual subscription. Pipedrive's own billing rules state that annual subscriptions are prepaid for the full year and are not refundable; canceling one keeps your access running until the end of the term you already paid for, rather than returning any money. Monthly subscriptions work differently: canceling one takes effect at your next billing date, so charges simply stop going forward. Pipedrive's per-seat billing compounds this: since every seat is charged whether or not it is filled, an annual plan locks in a full year of payment for seats a shrinking team no longer needs. If a predictable, easy-to-cancel bill matters more to you than the lower annual price, paying monthly on whichever plan you need is the safer default until you're confident you'll keep the account, and the same headcount, for a full year.

items.q: Does Pipedrive support SMS or texting?
items.a: No. Pipedrive has no native SMS-sending feature on any plan or add-on, and there's no per-message rate to budget for because there's no SMS product to buy in the first place. The 'texting' option some users find in Pipedrive's mobile app is only a shortcut that opens the phone's own messaging app with a contact's number already filled in; Pipedrive's own knowledge base describes it as a device-level convenience, not a feature it sends or bills for, and the exchange isn't logged back into Pipedrive's CRM records. A team that needs to text customers or leads from inside its CRM, with delivery logged automatically against the contact's record, needs either a separate texting tool connected through one of Pipedrive's app integrations, or a different CRM, such as GoHighLevel, that meters SMS as a built-in, billed feature.

items.q: What's the difference between Pipedrive's Lite and Growth plans?
items.a: Lite, at $24 a month per seat, has no email sync at all, meaning it can't connect to a mailbox, and no workflow automation of any kind, not even one automated step. Growth, at $49 a month per seat, adds both: one synced email mailbox per seat and up to 50 active automations shared company-wide, each allowing up to 3 if/else branching steps, plus 5 Pulse nurture sequences company-wide. Growth also roughly doubles Lite's per-seat capacity for leads and deals, from 2,500 up to 5,000, and raises the custom-field and reporting limits. Neither plan includes LeadBooster lead capture, Projects task management or Smart Docs e-signatures; on both, those stay separate paid add-ons, unlike on Premium and Ultimate, where all three come included. A solo rep who only logs calls and moves deals through stages by hand can stay on Lite; anyone who wants Pipedrive to send follow-up emails or trigger automations on its own needs Growth at minimum.
